Looking at this position, I need to identify the key features:

White has: King g1, Queen h4, Rooks d3 and e1, pawns on a2, c5, f2, g2, h2
Black has: King g8, Queen e5, Rooks b4 and f8, Knight f6, pawns on a5, d5, f5, g7, h7

The Black king is trapped on the back rank with limited escape squares. White's rook on d3 has a direct path to d8.

**The winning move is Rd8+!**

This forces Rxd8 (the only legal move), and then Rxd8# is checkmate—the king has no escape squares with the rook controlling d8 and f8, and pawns on g7 and h7 blocking escape.

**Coaching note:** Watch for back-rank weaknesses in your opponent's position. When their king is confined by its own pawns and you can sacrifice a rook to force them to recapture with their other piece, check if the recapture leads to mate. This tactical pattern—clearing the d-file to exploit the back rank—wins material or delivers mate instantly.
